source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Resting on fairly little established evidence of benefit despite being a commonly recommended self-management tool for asthma","B":"Being relevant mainly for clients with severe, poorly controlled asthma, rather than for asthma clients more broadly overall","C":"Taking the place of the ongoing provider follow-up the client would otherwise still need to attend regularly","D":"Guide the client in recognizing their current asthma control status and taking appropriate, timely action based on clear, individualized thresholds"}}
source_row.rationale: A written asthma action plan, using a color-coded zone system, helps guide the client in recognizing their current asthma control status and taking appropriate, timely action based on clear, individualized thresholds, valuable across a range of asthma severity, not only severe cases.
source_row.source_detail: Purpose of Written Asthma Action Plans
source_row.source_name: National Asthma Education and Prevention Program — Asthma Action Plans
source_row.stem: A nurse provides a client with asthma a written action plan, using a color-coded (green/yellow/red) zone system based on symptoms or peak flow readings. This tool helps:
